meta.area: mortality, causes of death, data reliability (China)
meta.notes: All WPP/WHO/IGME numbers were pulled from the official data files/APIs listed in each url field (WPP CSVs streamed and filtered to ISO3=CHN). Rates per 1000 live births unless stated.

life_expectancy.note: 2024 is the first projection year in WPP 2024; values computed from complete life tables
Bulletin published 2026-08-28; sex-specific values not reported
NBS says census life tables are 'process data' and not officially published (https://www.stats.gov.cn/hd/lyzx/zxgk/202409/t20240924_1956687.html); WPP 2024 for 2020: M 75.25, F 81.00, T 78.02

other_life_table_indicators.source: UN WPP 2024 complete life tables (computed: U5MR=1-l5/l0, 45q15=1-l60/l15)

qx.source: UN World Population Prospects 2024, complete (single-age) abridged life table, medium variant, China (LocID 156)
qx.note: Year 2024 is WPP's first projection year. WPP's 2024 IMR (M 7.0, F 5.7 per 1000) is higher than both its own 2023 estimate and UN IGME 2024 (M 4.3, F 3.9). If the game wants consistency with IGME/NHC, rescale q0 (and q1-q4) toward IGME values; adult ages unaffected.

child_mortality.source: UN IGME 2025 release (via UNICEF SDMX CME)

child_mortality.note: Conflicts with the bulletin's 3.8 for IMR; different reporting system/definition likely (unexplained)

child_mortality.source: China NHC statistical bulletin 2024 / NBS child-development monitoring report

child_mortality.note: Urban vs rural breakdown for 2023-2025 not found in accessible sources (it is in the China Health Statistical Yearbook tables). A Disease Surveillance study (https://www.jbjc.org/article/doi/10.3784/jbjc.202305090206) reports yearbook urban neonatal/infant/U5 rates HIGHER than rural for 2015-2021, which is implausible and suggests rural under-reporting.

causes_by_age.source: WHO Global Health Estimates 2021 (GHE 2021), China, deaths by cause and age, both sexes
causes_by_age.method: Shares = cause deaths / all-cause deaths summed over GHE age groups in each band (0=Y0T1; 1-14=Y1T4..Y10T14; 15-34=Y15T19..Y30T34; 35-59; 60-79; 80+=Y80T84+Y_GE85). 'perinatal_neonatal'=GHE 490 neonatal conditions; 'other_injuries' = all injuries minus road, drowning, self-harm, falls, natural disasters; 'other_cancers' = malignant neoplasms minus leukaemia, liver, lung, stomach, oesophagus, colorectal; 'copd_chronic_respiratory'=GHE 1170 respiratory diseases (COPD+asthma+other; LRI excluded); 'cirrhosis_liver_disease'=GHE 1230 (liver cancer listed separately); 'other' = residual so each band sums to 100. all_cancers_pct = sum of all cancer items.
caveats: GHE 2021 for China is modelled from DSP/vital-registration plus GBD inputs; COVID-19 is near zero in 2021 (3.8k deaths) but WHO GHE 2023 all-ages has 337k COVID deaths in China (https://xmart-api-public.who.int/DEX_CMS/GHE_FULL_DD).
IHME GBD 2021 cause-by-age for China was not retrievable without the interactive GBD Results Tool; not included.
China CDC DSP (中国死因监测数据集) national age-specific tables not accessible; only regional/older figures found.

suicide.source: WHO GHO MH_12 age-standardized suicide rate
WHO GHO SDGSUICIDE crude rate by age, both sexes
China CDC Weekly 2023;5(25):559-564, from China Health Statistical Yearbook
Disease Surveillance 2023;38(11):1391-1397, from DSP cause-of-death surveillance
BMC Public Health 2018 (DSP vs MoH vital registration, 2004-2014)
suicide.finding: DSP suicide rates higher than vital registration: IRR 1.18 national, 1.29 rural -> VR underestimates suicide

suicide.gap_note: WHO age-standardized (8.0 in 2023) is ~1.5x Chinese official age-standardized (5.25-5.71 in 2021); standard populations differ (WHO world standard vs Chinese census standard) so part of the gap is method, part is WHO's under-registration adjustment.

reliability.claim: About 19% of children aged 0-4 were unreported in the 2000 census, more than double the 1990 rate; rise linked to tougher birth-planning penalties after 1991; reported sex ratios inflated partly by hidden daughters.
Estimates of hidden births differ: Cai ~13% of female and 8% of male births in 2000 underreported; Shi & Kennedy argue 73% of 'missing girls' 1990-2010 are present but unregistered.
Infant mortality underestimated by at least 70% in most provinces in the 2010 census; adjusted sex gap in life expectancy larger than reported.
reliability.source: Li C., Mi H., Journal of Population Research 38(2):169-196, 2021

reliability.claim: 2010 census 1q0 ~4 per 1000 is implausibly low (>70% below the maternal-child surveillance figure); 2000 comparison: census 32.0, DSP 13.5, MCH surveillance 32.2 per 1000. DSP infant death under-registration 16-35% in the 1990s vs 13-14% all ages.
reliability.source: Biomed Environ Sci 2015; Rao et al. Popul Health Metr 2005

reliability.claim: WPP adjusts official census data for under-reporting of child and adult deaths and over-estimation of old-age mortality.
reliability.source: Missov, Nemeth, Li et al., HMD 5th Symposium presentation

reliability.claim: Census TFR 1.18 (2010) and 1.30 (2020); registered births widely thought under-counted, but recent work also notes possible OVER-reporting of annual NBS births and weak evidence of large continuous under-reporting; tempo/parity-adjusted TFR still below 1.5. UN WPP 2024 puts TFR at ~1.0 in 2023-2024.
reliability.source: Springer 2024; BMC Popul Health Metr 2022; UN WPP 2024

reliability.claim: Yi Fuxian (UW-Madison) argues China's 2020 population was ~1.28 billion, not the census 1.41 billion, and that population has shrunk since 2018; elsewhere claims >=130 million overcount driven by local subsidy incentives. Officials (NBS) have rejected this; demographers call parts of his work sloppy.
reliability.source: Reuters via nippon.com (2021); Korea Times op-ed (2022)

reliability.claim: 1.87 million (95% CI 0.71-4.43 million) excess deaths among people 30+ in the 2 months after zero-COVID ended, from university obituaries and Baidu searches; official count ~60,000 hospital COVID deaths to 12 Jan 2023.
reliability.source: Xiao H, Wang Z, Liu F, Unger JM. JAMA Netw Open 2023 (doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2023.30877, PMID 37615984)

reliability.claim: Urban-only ~917,000 (95% CI 425k-1.45m) vs ~81,000 official in-hospital deaths (Lipsitch group, CAE obituaries); at least 1.44 million (elite obituaries, J Popul Econ 2025); ~712,000 Dec 2022-Feb 2023 (search volume, Sci Rep 2023). Range ~0.7-1.9 million.
reliability.source: MIDAS; J Popul Econ 2025; Sci Rep 2023

reliability.claim: WHO GHE 2023 has 337k COVID deaths and 11.59m all-cause deaths in China in 2023 (NBS: 11.10m). UN WPP 2024 shows deaths 11.0m (2022) and 11.7m (2023) and only a small dip in e0 (78.2 -> 77.95).
National GDP growth 2008-2016 about 1.7 pp/yr lower than official (VAT-based re-estimate); sum of provincial GDP exceeded national GDP by 5-6 pp 2003-2016.
reliability.source: Chen, Chen, Hsieh, Song, Brookings Papers on Economic Activity, Spring 2019

reliability.claim: Night-lights evidence: autocracies overstate annual GDP growth by ~35% (factor 1.15-1.3); applies to non-democracies generally, not China-specific.
Liaoning governor admitted fiscal data falsified 2011-2014, inflated by at least 20% (up to 23% in 2014); Tianjin Binhai New Area cut its GDP by 33.4% (330 bn yuan) in 2018.
Vital registration under-estimated suicide relative to DSP (IRR 1.18 national, 1.29 rural, 2004-2014).

correction_factors.suggestion: Official NHC (4.0, 2024) ~= UN IGME (4.1, 2024) - IGME relies on the MCH surveillance system, so no large correction now; WPP's 6.4 is ~1.6x higher. Historic census IMR needs x3-x4 (>=70% under-reporting, 2010).
WHO age-standardized / Chinese official age-standardized ~ 8.0/5.3-5.7 ~ 1.4-1.5x; DSP/VR IRR 1.18-1.29.
Excess deaths ~10-30x the official hospital count (0.7-1.9m vs ~60-81k).

official_MEM.note: 2023/2024 full-year from search summaries citing MEM (Reuters, ministry year-end report); medium confidence

disasters.game_calibration: Recent baseline ~700-900 dead/missing per year (~0.5-0.6 per million per year; lifetime risk ~0.004-0.005%); fat tail from rare mega-earthquakes (2008 ~87k dead+missing). GHE assigns ~0.005% of deaths to natural disasters, so a per-year probability of ~6e-7 with a rare-catastrophe multiplier is reasonable.

gaps: IHME GBD 2021/2023 China cause-by-age death counts not retrieved (requires interactive GBD Results Tool); WHO GHE 2021 used instead.
China CDC 中国死因监测数据集 national age-specific cause shares not accessible online; not included.
Urban vs rural IMR/U5MR/MMR for 2023-2025 not found (yearbook tables not accessible).
NHC 2025 IMR conflict: bulletin 3.8 vs press conference 3.5 per 1000 (U5MR 5.4); unexplained.
WPP 2024 2024-projection IMR (6.4) is above WPP 2023 estimate (5.1) and IGME (4.1); qx[0] in the saved table may be too high vs official/IGME.
No official sex-specific life expectancy for 2024/2025; 2020 census values via secondary press source; NBS says census life tables are not officially published.
Economist COVID excess-death estimate could not be accessed (domain blocked); omitted.
Chinese official suicide rates by sex/age for 2022+ not found; 2021 age-standardized only.
